transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
The FBI is assisting authorities to determine a motive behind yesterday's mass shooting
at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon.
Police say a 16-year-old shot through locked doors at Silver Rail Elementary, killing three
children and a teacher.
An armed bystander followed the gunman into the school and fatally shot him.
Sariah Sharpe, whose 10-year-old attends the school, describes the confusion as parents
tried to reunite with their kids.
It was just really confusing and hard to know what to believe.
I can only say it's not the worst day of my life because I got to see his face, but not
everybody got to see their loved ones.
Hundreds gathered at a vigil last night to mourn the victims.
Trump heads to Georgia today to rally support for Republican candidates ahead of the November
midterm elections.
NPR's Ashley Lopez reports some swing voters in the state who backed him in 2024 say their
frustration with the president is shaping how they'll vote this year.
NPR observed focus groups with 12 voters in Georgia who voted for President Biden in 2020
and Trump in 2024.
11 now say they disapprove of the overall job Trump has been doing and 10 say they regret
voting for him.
Cynthia, an independent voter who participated under the condition her last name would not
be used, says this frustration is affecting how she's going to vote.
People that are aligned closely with him, I would not vote for because I haven't supported
what he's done so far.
And like I said, it's been a very big disappointment.
So I would probably lean toward people that are not aligned with him to vote for.
He said they hope a mix of power in Washington will create some stability.
Ashley Lopez, NPR News.
Several Palestinians and an American photojournalist for The Washington Post were beaten and injured
by settlers in the Israeli occupied West Bank today.
The Washington Post said the attack happened when Palestinians were trying to gather their
olive harvest.
NPR's Adil al-Shalji reports it comes at a time where violence in the West Bank has seen
a sharp rise.
The Washington Post said that the Israeli settlers set Palestinian olive groves on fire
and hurled stones using slingshots.
It said that veteran photojournalist Heidi Levine was wearing a protective vest clearly
marked with the word "press."
In an Instagram post, Levine said a group of settlers knocked her to the ground.
They just kept kicking me and kicking me probably 50 times.
The paper said she was receiving medical care and was safe in a statement The Washington
Post called for a "thorough investigation."
The Israeli police condemned the attacks and said it would investigate.
Witnesses said Israeli soldiers did not stop the settler assaults.
Hadil al-Shalji, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Emergency crews in Southern California are working to contain a wildfire.
Cal Fire says the blaze in Malibu has burned about 147 acres and is about 17 percent contained.
It broke out yesterday in the Santa Monica Mountains.
Forecasters say strong Santa Ana winds and low humidity are making conditions dangerous.
Electric automaker Tesla has unveiled a new sports car.
The EV uses built-in thrusters to leap over obstacles and can go from 0 to 60 in under
one second.
And PR's John Ruich has the details.
The Tesla Roadster is a collaboration between Tesla and SpaceX, and CEO Elon Musk unveiled
it at a SpaceX rocket test center in Texas.
It has 10 built-in nozzles that use ultra-high pressure air that can propel the car down
the road or make it jump into the air and do a barrel roll.
It also has fans that can push it down toward the road for better traction.
Tesla has been investing in self-driving technology, and Musk said the Roadster would eventually
be the only manually driven car in the lineup.
The angular sports car, he said, is better than any James Bond car and will enter production
in 2028.
He added, though, that it's not necessarily safety optimized and might not be legal.
John Ruich, NPR News.
Areas of central and southwest Mexico are bracing for Hurricane Trudy.
It's a major category three storm with top sustained winds of 120 miles per hour.
The National Hurricane Center in Florida says Trudy will remain a major storm when it moves
close to the coast this weekend.
This is NPR.

topics.text: FBI assists probe into motive for Bend, Oregon elementary school shooting that killed four
Trump heads to Georgia to rally support for Republican candidates before midterms
Georgia swing voters who backed Trump in 2024 express disapproval and regret, focus groups show
Israeli settlers beat Palestinians and Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine in West Bank
Cal Fire battles Malibu wildfire in Santa Monica Mountains, 17 percent contained
Tesla and SpaceX unveil Roadster sports car with built-in thrusters, Elon Musk says
Hurricane Trudy, a major Category 3 storm, threatens central and southwest Mexico coast
